concept.title: Podcast production workflow
concept.shortdesc: A typical order of work for a spoken-word podcast: prepare, record, clean up, level and export.

conbody.p: is a popular choice for podcast production because it is free, cross-platform and capable of professional results. This topic outlines a typical workflow.

ol.li: Test your microphone levels; aim for peaks around -12 to leave headroom.
Record in a quiet room with little echo.
Use a pop filter to soften plosive sounds (p, b, t).
Set the project to 44,100 Hz and 32-bit float for editing flexibility.
Record a few seconds of silence at the start for a noise profile.
Press R to start recording; monitor the meter and stay out of the red.
If you make a mistake, pause briefly and say the sentence again; you will cut the first attempt later.

section.title: Post-production
section.p: Process the audio in this order (see for each effect's parameters):

ol.li: Noise reduction: remove background noise using the noise profile from the silence.
Editing: trim mistakes, long pauses and false starts.
Normalization: bring the peak level to -1.0 dB.
Compression: even out volume differences (threshold -18 dB, ratio 3:1).
Export: MP3 at 128 kbps mono for distribution, by hand or from a script ().

section.title: Getting started with podcasting
section.p: If you are new to podcasting, start simple: record, trim the beginning and end, and export as MP3. As you gain experience, explore noise reduction, compression and the other effects to polish your sound.
